title: Night Shift at the Lighthouse (example)
subject: Claudia: a 28-year-old Caucasian American woman with a grown-up angular face, defined cheekbones and a strong jawline, pale skin and light freckles, a glossy black blunt jaw-length bob with heavy straight bangs and one clay-orange streak through the bangs, a small flat clay-orange eight-pointed star hair clip

looks.keeper: wearing a heavy navy wool coat over a cream fisherman's jumper, dark trousers and black boots

world: The world is the lamp room of a small lighthouse at night: a great glass lens turning slowly, brass rails, a wooden desk with an old radio, rain on the windows, filmed on 35mm in warm practical light.
manner: warm and open: she enjoys singing to us

S1.prompt: A cinematic film still: the lamp room of a small lighthouse at night, the great glass lens behind her, a wooden desk with an old radio at her side, rain on the windows. She is the woman on the reference sheet in the first image: the same face, {subject}. She is {look:keeper}. One natural pose, her expression warm and at ease; her face is unblocked, her lips closed. Warm practical light from the lamp. A medium shot from the waist up. The picture fills the whole frame edge to edge. Shot on 35mm film, fine grain. No text, no letters, no logos.

Q1-end.prompt: The same photograph from the same camera, a moment later: the radio's amber dial glows brighter and its needle has swung across to the far end of the dial. Nothing else changes: the same framing, light and colours.

shots.goal: Claudia, the keeper, tells us how she keeps the light running.
shots.place: the lamp room, the great lens behind her, the desk and the radio at her side
shots.camera: A slow push-in from the waist-up view of @Image1 to a close shot; no cuts.
timeline: rest
she turns from the lens to us and smiles
she pats the old radio on the desk, then opens her hand toward the lens
she leans on the brass rail and nods out at the dark water
rest
she glances back at the turning lens

shots.goal: She reads the weather off the sea instead of the forecast.
shots.place: at the rain-streaked window, the sea far below
shots.camera: Locked medium shot as in @Image1; no cuts.
timeline: rest
she wipes a circle in the fogged glass with her sleeve
she taps the window twice where the forecast card is pinned, and shrugs
she turns her head to us and tips it toward the stairs, a smile in her eyes
rest
she lets the curtain fall back

shots.goal: A close view of an old valve radio on a wooden desk at night: its dial glows as voices come over the air.
shots.first: the radio's cloth speaker, its round amber dial and a mug beside it, lit by the lighthouse lamp
events: 0-1s: the radio sits still; rain runs on the window behind it.
1-3s: the amber dial brightens and its needle swings slowly across the stations; the speaker cloth trembles.
3-4s: the needle settles; the glow stays.
shots.camera: Locked close view as in the first frame; no cuts.

shots.goal: One answer in the call and answer: she answers the radio.
shots.place: close on her at the desk, the radio in front of her
shots.camera: Locked close shot as in @Image1; no cuts.
timeline: rest
she listens to the radio, eyes bright
she leans toward the radio and points down through the floor at the sea below
rest
she sits back with a closed-lip smile

shots.goal: She listens to the second question from the radio.
shots.place: the lamp room, the lens turning behind her
events: 0-2s: she looks up at the great lens as it turns, listening; her lips stay closed.
2-4s: she rests one hand on the brass rail and turns back toward us, about to answer.
shots.camera: Locked medium shot as in @Image1; no cuts.

shots.goal: Her last answer: she keeps the lights, every night.
shots.place: on the gallery outside the lamp room, the beam sweeping over her
shots.camera: A slow crane up and back from the medium shot of @Image1 as the beam passes; one continuous move, no cuts.
timeline: rest
she steps out onto the gallery into the wind
she lifts one arm toward the sweeping beam as it passes over her
rest
she lowers her arm and laughs into the wind
